text:
ashwin: heads-up — noticed a new failure mode in 16-node TP runs after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. multiple jobs hit allreduce stalls and ranks desyncing during step 120-150. logs show repeated timeouts.

leo: +1 saw it on a canary cluster at 03:10 UTC. repro steps: run 16-node TP with batch packing enabled and dynamic-kernel routing on. it hangs ~2-3 minutes then allreduce times out for one rank.

olivia: throwing the profiler at it now. initial flamegraph looks like allreduce is serialized on a single thread for some ranks — comm/compute overlap basically collapsed.

ashwin: paste from one job's stderr: 
```
E: Allreduce operation timed out at rank 7 (peer 12 unresponsive)
E: Rendezvous waiting for group 0: ranks [0..15], last seen heartbeat 00:02:14 ago
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/runtime/serving/launcher.py", line 412, in step
    sync_allreduce(tensors)
  File "/opt/runtime/comm/allreduce.py", line 89, in sync_allreduce
    raise AllReduceTimeoutError
AllReduceTimeoutError: timed out
```

tang: I instrumented KV cache metrics. there's a big spike in `kvcache.evictions/sec` right before the hang, correlated with increased microbatch packing. looks like the kernel selector changed packing boundaries which forces cache thrash across TP ranks.

leo: hmm, so two knobs changed: kernel routing now prefers `tensor_block_v2` for medium seq lengths, and batching now tries to pack uneven sequences into 3 microbatches instead of 2. those together could change memory alignment and cause some ranks to allocate different buffer sizes. if buffer sizes don't match across ranks we could see allreduce shape mismatches or rendezvous stalls.

olivia: confirmed discrepant buffer shapes in perf traces: rank 3/7 had `KV len=248` while peers had `KV len=256` for same step. mismatch originates from packing decision just before KV cache write.

ken: can we reproduce with a smaller node count? try 4-node with same sequence distribution. if it's deterministic it should fail faster. also include `--trace-kv` flag I added last week.

ashwin: repro on 4-node in ~30s with `--trace-kv`. attaching shortened trace here: 
```
[rank0] pack->batches: [128,128]  kv_write: len=256
[rank3] pack->batches: [64,64,64,56] kv_write: len=248
[rendezvous] expect_len=256 seen_len=248 -> wait_for_peer(3)
```

tang: this explains the eviction spike — narrower writes cause more frequent flushes. kernel selector change altered block rounding causing per-rank divergence when sequence lengths vary.

leo: likely root cause: non-deterministic packing algorithm when `batching.heuristic=dynamic` interacts with new kernel alignment assumptions. code path at `kernel_selector.py:choose_kernel` assumes global alignment invariant which is now violated.

infra-bot: deploy alert: canary group 7 showed 12% failure rate for TP runs after 2026-03-16T03:00 UTC. rollback recommended if more than 5% impact.

olivia: immediate mitigation: force `batching.heuristic=fixed` OR pin kernel to `tensor_block_v1` until we patch the selector to respect packing boundaries. both options reduce throughput but prevent hangs.

ashwin: I'll roll a hotfix that: 1) disables dynamic packing for TP multi-node by default, 2) adds an assertion in kernel selector to validate per-rank buffer sizes before entering allreduce.

ken: I'll open a perf-run job that measures comm/compute overlap before/after hotfix. assign me to the PR review.

leo: follow-up tasks:
- add unit test that simulates skewed seq lengths across TP ranks (olivia)
- add CI e2e with `--trace-kv` enabled for multi-node runs (ken)
- revert kernel-selector heuristic change and re-land with alignment checks (ashwin)

tang: one more note: we should add a lightweight pre-allreduce handshake that validates tensor shapes and logs offending rank immediately (avoid long rendezvous waits). can implement as opt-in for now.

ashwin: agreed. i'll push a short-term handshake that fails fast and emits structured log `kvcache_shape_mismatch` so SRE can auto-detect.

olivia: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/4821 — includes debug traces and the temp handshake. please review.

leo: triage summary: root cause = kernel-selector + dynamic packing interaction -> per-rank KV buffer shape divergence -> allreduce/rendezvous stalls. mitigation = pin packing or kernel; long-term = align kernel selector invariants and add handshake + CI tests.

ashwin: tagging @sre on pager rotation in case any canary jobs still alarm. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

infra-bot: actioned: canary rollback scheduled in 10m unless PR merged with hotfix.

ken: will send perf results once CI completes.

(took place over ~8 minutes, logs and traces attached to the PR)
